# Browser deployment matrix

This matrix is generated from the pinned Playwright 1.62.1 headless Linux qualification run over candidate `2268d2b0ff831f7689d269ade027057ea533224d` and the single shipped simd128 AudioWorklet artifact `df4a880085f673d6ba04f9bc26506fbe7c69350d53e7ac9b7843bda332444479`. The version shown is the lowest version qualified by this run; older versions are unqualified, not implicitly supported.

| Browser engine | Qualified version floor | Attestation outcome | SIMD gate | AudioWorklet boot | Native corpus digest | Live controls (#137) | Observation (#143) | 100 ms main-thread stall |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| chromium | 151.0.7922.34 | simd128 supported | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| webkit | 26.5 | simd128 supported | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |

The observation gate (issue #143) subscribes to the compressor's declared gain-reduction tap, requires at least one `miso.meter.v1` frame whose `trackGrDb` carries a **positive** magnitude the app can read without clamping, requires `masterGrDb` to be the designated track's own reading, requires the reported windows to advance monotonically and tile with no gap, requires a never-armed tap to publish no reduction over at least one frame, requires (issue #1535), on one real `AudioContext` resumed by one trusted click, that an acknowledged unsubscribe leaves no reduction in any later frame while at least 48 later frames still carry the fed signal, and requires the armed and unarmed renders of the same sixteen blocks to produce **bit-identical audio** -- arming a declared tap may not move a sample. The live-control gate (issue #137) applies one `SET_CONTROL` matrix retarget, requires the rendered output to equal the declared half-gain result bit for bit, and requires at least one decimated `miso.meter.v1` frame whose master peak is a real observation of that output plus at least one windowed `miso.telemetry.v1` frame. The structural-edit gates (issue #1295) run on this page without cross-origin isolation, the module's `single` mode: one `miso.control.v1` `SESSION_REPLACE` with a replacement document (the browser fixture plus an unmuted -6 dB EQ track on the same source) is committed on the rebuild path, the applied-revision watermark reports it in effect from the swap block with the outcome exact, no source block underruns, the capture equals the shipped module's own render of the same frame and document under Node bit for bit, and the host status counts exactly one blocking rebuild and a growth of `singleModeControlAllocations` (decision 15, D15-10); a replacement by the 1 MiB boot-ceiling document is committed, counted and adopted, and its memory growth is reported against the boot's projection, never pinned. The stall gate injects at least 100 ms of main-realm blocking after prefilling the 5120-frame stall source ring, now with the control path and the meter fold both live across the fault, and requires bit-exact, dropout-free, frame-aligned output. `miso.unsupported.v1` is the only qualified refusal for a browser without simd128.

Playwright's browser builds are qualification targets, not claims about branded Chrome or Safari builds: the qualified engines are desktop Chromium and WebKit only. Firefox is not a supported browser (owner ruling 2026-10-25, #2092). iOS Safari is not qualified: the iPhone check (#1331) is closed as not planned (owner decision 2026-10-27). Re-run the matrix before lowering a deployment floor or changing Playwright. The recorded run above is the last release's artifact, recorded before the module was built on one imported shared `WebAssembly.Memory` (issue #1380); between releases it is not re-recorded (docs/RELEASE.md). Until the next release re-records it, the shared-memory module is qualified by the per-change browser legs (the same gates, chromium and webkit, on every pull request), with one instance per memory, on a page without cross-origin isolation (the module's `single` mode) and, for the PCM feed row, on an isolated page. Two instances on one memory (a control Worker beside the render-only worklet, #1332) are not qualified.
